lessonTitle: 29. Properties and graphs of sine and cosine
lessonTitleEnglish: Properties and graphs of sine and cosine
unit: Algebra · Chapter 4. Trigonometric functions and equations
source: Based on the topics of the Armenian grade 10 mathematics textbooks (advanced stream)

stages.headline: The graph of y = sin x is a sinusoid: D = ℝ, E = [−1; 1], odd, periodic with T = 2π, zeros x = πk.
stages.headlineEnglish: The graph of y = sin x is a sinusoid: D = ℝ, E = [−1; 1], odd, periodic with T = 2π, zeros x = πk.

stages.headline: The graph of y = cos x is the sinusoid shifted π/2 to the left, since cos x = sin(x + π/2); cos x is even with zeros x = π/2 + πk.
stages.headlineEnglish: The graph of y = cos x is the sinusoid shifted π/2 to the left, since cos x = sin(x + π/2); cos x is even with zeros x = π/2 + πk.

stages.headline: sin x increases on [−π/2 + 2πk; π/2 + 2πk] and reaches its maximum 1 at x = π/2 + 2πk; cos x reaches 1 at x = 2πk.
stages.headlineEnglish: sin x increases on [−π/2 + 2πk; π/2 + 2πk] and reaches its maximum 1 at x = π/2 + 2πk; cos x reaches 1 at x = 2πk.
